Commentary.Commentary: Windies' bowling was not up to the mark. They did bowl well in patches but never created enough pressure. Kemar Roach was the pick of the bowlers as he tested the batsmen with his pace and accuracy. Their spinners, although picked late wickets, were a major disappointment on a helpful deck. Now, they have a big first innings total in front of them and will have to bat out of their skin against the army of Bangladesh spinners. Stay tuned, their reply will commence soon.

Exceptional batting performance by the home team. They won the toss on Day 1 and adopted a slow approach initially. Runs were hard to come by but they stuck around and concentrated on forming partnerships. Debutant Shadman Islam was the star yesterday as he impressed everyone with his composure and shot selection. The hosts switched gears this morning and then started to score briskly. Shakib started it all and Liton Das took it forward. Amidst all this, Mahmudullah held one end and anchored the innings with a hard-fought century. He was involved in quite a few handy stands and the best one was his 111-run association with the skipper. The efforts of the lower order cannot be undermined either as they helped in taking the total past the 500-run mark.

OUT! There is some spike! Windies get lucky with this wicket. There wasn't much excitement shown in the appeal and after knowing the third umpire's verdict, Jomel Warrican has a relieved smile on his face. A nicely tossed up delivery outside off, enticing the batsman to go for a drive. Mehidy commits himself into the shot but is beaten as the ball spins away past his bat. Dowrich collects the ball and lets out a muted appeal initially. Then, they go for the DRS more as an afterthought. The replays roll in and they show that it has taken a faint outside edge. For a moment, we thought it was due to the bottom of the bat brushing the surface but the other angle confirmed that the spike was generated due to the outside edge. A terrific review in the end. First success for Warrican, Windies claim the eighth wicket but it's Bangladesh in the driver's seat.

Windies started well initially but once Mahmudullah and Shakib started to counterattack, they went flat. Kemar Roach once again was the best bowler on show but he didn't receive much support from his partners. Given the nature of the pitch, their spinners have been a big disappointment. The tourists are staring down the barrel and need a big effort from hereon to turn things around. It's advantage Bangladesh going into the break. Do join us in a short while for the afternoon session.

If Day 1 was about sharing sessions, Bangladesh have been selfish on Day 2. Came out with a very positive intent and hammered 128 runs in the morning in spite of losing Shakib Al Hasan. They find themselves in the driver's seat now and will have to thank the ongoing partnership between Liton Das and Mahmudullah. The pair has been ruthless, Liton in particular, and as a result, Bangladesh are only 13 short of the 400-run mark.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the second Test between Bangladesh and Windies at Mirpur. We head to Day 2 with this Test match very much in balance. The morning session will be crucial as Windies might decide to take the second new ball immediately. Given the way this surface has behaved, Bangladesh will hope to bat big in their first innings and take their total close to 400, if not more. It promises to be yet another fascinating day on Saturday. Do join us at 0930 local (0330 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

The tourists picked up a couple of wickets late in the afternoon session and then removed Mushfiqur Rahim soon after the Tea break in a bid to gain an upper hand. But Shakib and Mahmudullah made sure to see off the day's play safely. The Bangladeshi skipper did get a reprieve on 31 when an lbw decision wasn't reviewed by Windies. Zooming on the bowling performance, Kemar Roach bowled his heart out while Sherman Lewis also looked in rhythm in the spell where he sent Rahim packing. Roston Chase and Devendra Bishoo were among the wickets but Jomel Warrican was a major disappointment.

Earlier, Bangladesh won the all-important toss and had no hesitation in batting first. Debutant Shadman Islam and Soumya Sarkar provided them with a steady start but then Roston Chase hunted down the latter with a lovely off spinning delivery. Another partnership developed after that but just before the Lunch break, Kemar Roach picked up the prized scalp of Mominul Haque. Mohammad Mithun and Shadman joined forces to raise a 64-run stand post Lunch and the debutant went on to notch up a fine half century, thereby impressing everyone with his temperament.

End of an absorbing day of Test cricket! We witnessed three well-fought sessions. Whenever Bangladesh looked like running away with the show, Windies bounced back by picking wickets. The first two sessions were shared but the last one owing to the 69-run partnership between Shakib and Mahmudullah gave Bangladesh the edge.

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

A session which will fall in the category of shared one due to the two late wickets. Bangladesh batted without any issues in the first hour post Lunch where the pair of Mithun and Shadman raised a fifty partnership. Devendra Bishoo struck twice after that to remove both the batsmen and provided Windies with a reason to smile. The Bangladeshi debutant was unlucky to miss out on a century but did enough to prove his mettle. The tourists are doing well to be patient as they are not giving away easy runs. Also, their overrate has to be praised. 27 overs more left in the day's play. Do join us in a short while for all the action.

Windies didn't bowl badly but they weren't too threatening, particularly the pacers. Also, compared to the regular spinners, Warrican and Bishoo, Chase looked more penetrative. They would like to get better with their lines and lengths post Lunch and create further inroads. The visitors already have been lucky twice that two promising partnerships got broken just in time. They just can't afford to let the batsmen settle in on this surface. Having said that, the Bangladeshi debutant, Shadman Islam, has looked quite compact in his first outing and will like to make it count. Do join us in a short while for the second session.

Excellent end to the session for the touring team. Although it was owned by the hosts until the last ball. They won a good toss and their openers laid a strong platform. But just before the Drinks break, they lost Soumya Sarkar. The pitch was offering plenty of spin and bounce right from the beginning, and Roston Chase was the one to provide the initial breakthrough. Yet another partnership developed after that which also ended before the break. Losing Mominul Haque is a body blow to Bangladesh but they bat deep and given the way this surface is playing, the home team would not be too disheartened.

Drinks break. A good hour of play this morning. The pitch is already taking turn and it's going to be a fascinating battle. Windies will be knowing that Bangladesh have packed their side with spinners and that's why the visitors will have to restrict them to a low first innings total. Meanwhile, Mominul Haque has joined Shadman in the middle.

OUT! First breakthrough for Windies and it's Roston Chase who has provided it. He was getting good spin and bounce from the surface and utilizes it to his advantage this time. He bowls a loopy one outside off, Sarkar is lured into the drive but it curls away with extra lift to catch the shoulder of the bat. A simple take for Shai Hope at first slip who jumps to pouch it easily. A good looking partnership is brought to an abrupt end and Bangladesh's opening woes continue.
Loopy and full on off, Sarkar presses forward and pushes it back to the bowler.

Keeps his length full this time and Islam defends it off his front foot. Warrican begins his spell with a maiden.
Pushes it quicker through the air and lands it on middle, Shadman is on the back foot in defense.

This one is on the shorter side outside off, Sarkar gets back and plays a late cut, almost off the keeper's gloves. Places it past first slip and the backward point fielder gives it the chase. Two added to the total.

Once again Chase bowls it slower through the air but wider outside off, Sarkar drives it square of the wicket on the off side and finds the gap. The sweeper cover fielder runs across to his right to stop the ball and they take a couple.

FOUR! Wow, what a drive! Sherman serves a juicy half-volley outside off, Shadman gets on the front foot and crunches his drive through extra cover for a beautiful boundary.
Full and angling into the batsman, Shadman keeps his eyes on the ball and defends it down safely. That one stayed a little low also.
Lands it fuller than the last time and bowls it outside off, Islam brings his bat down in defense and it goes off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Well played! Short in length and outside off, Shadman stays on the back foot and slaps it through the vacant region between gully and point for a boundary. It was a bit aerial but in the gap.

That's more like it. Pitch it full and around off. There is ample spin along with extra bounce. Sarkar flirts with it and is beaten.

Quicker through the air, an arm ball around middle and leg. Islam goes back and turns it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.

That's not the length to bowl when you getting good bounce and spin from the surface. Chase drags his length short and bowls it outside off, Sarkar rocks back and cuts it past the backward point fielder. He chases it down as the ball slows down before the rope. They take three runs.
A touch short and angling into the batsman from outside off, Shadman pushes himself inside the crease as he defends it back to the bowler.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Angles in a full length ball on off, Islam gets behind the line and defends it from the outer half of his bat.

Sherman digs in a short delivery, Islam stands tall inside the crease, fetches it from outside off and pulls it all along the ground through mid-wicket for a run.
Good length delivery in the zone outside off, holding its line, Shadman covers his stumps and then shoulders arms.

Goes slower through the air and bowls it full on off, Sarkar drives but finds the cover fielder.

Pulls his length back a bit and lands it around off. It spins away a touch with extra bounce and Sarkar goes on the back foot to defend it.

Nice shot again. Looked stylish. Lewis delivers a back of a length ball on off, Islam lifts his front leg up and pulls it in front of square leg for a run.
On a length around off, Islam defends it off his back foot. Looking quite compact, the debutant.
Shot! Lewis looks for some movement from the surface and for that he overpitches outside off. Shadman gets forward and drives it delightfully past the diving cover fielder. A couple of runs taken.
Another length ball on off, Islam keeps himself glued inside the crease as he blocks it down safely.

It's time to get underway. Soumya Sarkar has a new opening partner in Shadman Islam. So two left-handers will be opening. Kemar Roach to begin proceedings with the brand new ball. Two slips in place. Here we go...

Pitch report - The outfield looks good and quick. The surface looks good as well. It's hard with a nice covering of grass. Seems like good batting conditions. Lots of runs to be scored. Win the toss and bat first, that's the way to go. No-brainer really.

Toss - Shakib Al Hasan wins the all-important toss and no prizes for guessing, BANGLADESH WILL BAT. A big relief for the home team as Mushfiqur Rahim is passed fit to play, however, he will not keep. In comes Liton Das to don the gloves and to accommodate him, Mustafizur Rahman is sacrificed. The other change being Shadman Islam, who will make his debut in place of inured Imrul Kayes. For Windies, there is one obvious change - Shannon Gabriel is out as he will be serving his one-match suspension from the ICC. He is replaced by Shermon Lewis, who is just one Test match old.

Warm welcome ladies and gentlemen for the second Test match between Bangladesh and Windies at the Shere Bangla National Stadium, Mirpur. The hosts registered a comprehensive win in the last match and would be eyeing to take revenge for their last series loss in West Indies with a 2-0 scoreline. Their spinners once again will be the hot property and it's needless to say, how the Windies batsmen deal with them will decide the fate of this game. A few injuries and suspension will result in some change in combinations in both the sides and it will be interesting to find out which team gets affected the most. Stay tuned for more updates...
